pr_title: fix: right-click paste for images in clipboard (Issue #8826)
pr_body:
This PR fixes the issue with pasting images from the clipboard using the right-click context menu. Previously, users were unable to paste copied images from the clipboard when using the right-click action, which hindered the usability of the application. While pasting with `Ctrl + V` was functioning correctly, the right-click custom paste option was not working as intended. This fix addresses that issue and improves the overall user experience.

### Related Issue
Fixes #8826.

Hello @Mrazator @ad1992 @dwelle ,
had a quick question. 

When we paste from the right click, we refer to `createPasteEvent` in `clipboard.ts` while when pasting from Keyboard, we use `pasteFromClipboard` in `App.tsx`. Why is that? 

Why can't we move the part that pastes to a seperate function in maybe utils or somewhere else? from where both the files can call it? 

I understand that one is an event and other isn't but when I did some simple debugging, I found that the files in the createPasteEvent are undefined for some reason but when I check the same in `App.tsx` it is well formatted and contains data. 

Note: Just a rookie here trying to learn, contribute to Open Source with not much indepth knowledge of coding of this project. Also, it would be grateful if you could tell me how to debug excalidraw in VS Code.

> When we paste from the right click, we refer to createPasteEvent in clipboard.ts while when pasting from Keyboard, we use pasteFromClipboard in App.tsx. Why is that?

We use `pasteFromClipboard`, also when pasting manually through context menu and the input is result from `createPasteEvent`. If the question is why we are running `createPasteEvent`, then it's likely due to the browser emitting the event automatically on `ctrl/cmd + v`, while we need to "emit" it manually when triggered through the context menu.

> Also, it would be grateful if you could tell me how to debug excalidraw in VS Code.

The most straightforward is debugging through the Chrome devtools (opening "Sources" tab, clicking on file you want to debug and adding a breakpoint).
